scope: Corollary 5.2 (Reusing the families) of the manuscript “A Low-Space Algorithm for Worst-Case Subset Sum” (preprints/A-Low-Space-Algorithm-for-Worst-Case-Subset-Sum-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 138 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 88f951cb233cf765), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a finite list of checks satisfying the input conditions of Lemma 5.1, with common block parameters, and let Ncheck = X checks (|L| + |R|). The list may itself be random, provided that, conditional on the list and its parameters, the four families have the independent distributions (25). In the ideal experiment, the expected total check work conditional on the list and its parameters is at most W0 = Nchecku22 2(1−h∗)m . Preprocessing is paid once. Processing checks one at a time uses the check workspace of Lemma 5.1, in addition to any storage retained by the caller. For any 0 < δ < 1, total check work exceeds W0/δ with probability at most δ. Suppose a designated check and a solution pair in it are also chosen, and that conditional on the list, its parameters, and these choices, the families still have the independent distributions (25). Then with probability at least 1 − 4e−10 − δ the pair is covered and the total check work is at most W0/δ.
